summary:
[  edit  ]
The Fit  SOP  fits a Spline curve to a sequence of points or a Spline surface to an m X n mesh of points.
Any type of face or surface represents a valid input. The Fit  SOP  looks only at the control vertices (CVs) of the primitives, treating the CVs as data points to run the fit through. For example, if a cubic NURBS surface and a mesh have the same number of rows and columns and identical points, they will yield an identical fit because the Spline bases of the input NURBS surface are ignored.
The Fit  SOP  generates two types of outputs: primitives that roughly follow the path of the data points without necessarily going through the data points; and primitives that touch all the data points. The first type, known as "approximation", is used primarily to extract a lean, smooth shape from a heavy data set, lending itself well to data reduction. The second type, known as "interpolation", often serves as a smoothing tool for paths that must go through specified target positions.

parameters.label: Method
parameters.name: method
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specifies one of two fitting styles: approximation or interpolation. Each style has a number of parameters that are accessible from the respective folder. For more information see the Approximation and Interpolation pages below.

parameters.label: Primitive  Type
parameters.name: type
parameters.description: ⊞  - The output of the Fit  SOP  is a NURBS or Bzier primitive. All input faces are fitted to Spline curves, and all input surfaces are fitted to spline surfaces. The resulting shapes are identical whether created as NURBS or as Bzier primitives.

parameters.label: Connectivity
parameters.name: surftype
parameters.description: ⊞  - This option is used to select the type of surface, when using a Mesh  Primitive  Type.

parameters.label: Rows
parameters.name: rows
parameters.description: Creates horizontal lines.

parameters.label: Columns
parameters.name: cols
parameters.description: Creates vertical lines.

parameters.label: Rows and Columns
parameters.name: rowcol
parameters.description: Both Rows and Columns. Looks like Quads in wire frame display, but all polygons are open (if the primitive type is polygon).

parameters.label: Triangles
parameters.name: triangles
parameters.description: Build the grid with Triangles.

parameters.label: Quadrilaterals
parameters.name: quads
parameters.description: Generates sides composed of quadrilaterals (default).

parameters.label: Alternating Triangles
parameters.name: alttriangles
parameters.description: Generates triangles that are opposed; similar to the Triangles option.

parameters.label: U Order
parameters.name: orderu
parameters.description: If the input is a face, this is the order of the Spline curve to be generated. If the input is a surface, this is the order of the fitted spline surface in the U parametric direction.

parameters.label: V Order
parameters.name: orderv
parameters.description: If the input is a surface, this is the order of the fitted Spline surface in the V parametric direction. The V order is irrelevant if the input is a face.

parameters.label: Approximation fitting is used primarily to generate a lean, smooth shape from a dense data set. The result is a primitive that approximates the positions and attributes of the data points but does not necessarily touch these points. The only points the fitted curve or surface goes through are the end
parameters.description: points of the data set. If the fitted primitive is required to go through all the points, fitting by interpolation is the answer.

parameters.label: Tolerance
parameters.name: tol
parameters.description: This is the primary precision factor in approximation fitting. The smaller the tolerance, the closer the fit and the higher the number of generated vertices. If a small tolerance causes unwanted twists or contortions in the fitted primitive, it may help to vary the Spline order and/or enable the Multiple Knots flag.

parameters.label: Smoothness
parameters.name: smooth
parameters.description: For a set tolerance, the smoothness factor allows for more or less roundness in the generated shape. If this parameter is zero, it does not mean that the fit will be sharp. It simply indicates that no additional smoothing is required past the level of smoothness already achieved with the given tolerance.

parameters.label: U Multiple Knots
parameters.name: multipleu
parameters.description: Sometimes the data set has sharp bends that must be preserved in the fitted shape. In this case, inserting multiple knots in the areas of sharp curvature will usually produce the right effect. Sometimes, however, the simulated sharpness induces unwanted twists immediately before or after the corner. Lowering the Spline order and/or reducing the tolerance may help diminish this side-effect.

parameters.label: V Multiple Knots
parameters.name: multiplev
parameters.description: Sometimes the data set has sharp bends that must be preserved in the fitted shape. In this case, inserting multiple knots in the areas of sharp curvature will usually produce the right effect. Sometimes, however, the simulated sharpness induces unwanted twists immediately before or after the corner. Lowering the Spline order and/or reducing the tolerance may help diminish this side-effect.

parameters.label: Scope
parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: ⊞  -  Scope  establishes the interpolation method.

parameters.label: Global
parameters.name: global
parameters.description: Global interpolation take the whole data set into account at once and generates exactly as many CVs as data points is it given.

parameters.label: Local (Curves Only)
parameters.name: local
parameters.description: Local interpolation takes a more geometric approach, building the curve or surface one span at a time, using only local data at each step. The local method generates more CVs than the number of data points it is given, but it usually yields a tighter fit than the global method. The local approach is also less computationally expensive than the global one, and handles cusps and local perturbations better. Local interpolation is available only for curves.

parameters.label: Breakpoints
parameters.name: breakpnt
parameters.description: Breakpoint interpolation is a variant of global interpolation that satisfies the requirement that the locations of data points coincide with the breakpoints of the generated curve. The breakpoints of a Spline curve are the image of the Spline basis on the curve. Breakpoint interpolation is available only for curves.

parameters.label: U Data  Parameter
parameters.name: dataparmu
parameters.description: ⊞  - Specifies the parameterization of the data in the U direction (the only direction if the input is a curve). The data parameterization can be uniform, chord length, or centripetal.

parameters.label: V Data  Parameter
parameters.name: dataparmv
parameters.description: ⊞  - V data parameterization is identical to U data parameterization, but it affects the V direction when the input is a surface. It is not used when the input is a face.

parameters.label: U Wrap
parameters.name: closeu
parameters.description: ⊞  - This menu determines whether the fitted curve should be closed, or whether the fitted surface should be wrapped in the U parametric direction. The options are to open (Off), close (On), or inherit the closure type from the input primitive.

parameters.label: V Wrap
parameters.name: closev
parameters.description: ⊞  - This menu determines whether the fitted surface should be wrapped in the V parametric direction. The options are to open (Off), close (On), or inherit the closure type from the input primitive. V Wrap is ignored when the input is a face.

parameters.label: Fit Corners
parameters.name: corners
parameters.description: Specifies whether corners in the data should be preserved when doing local curve interpolation.

parameters.label: num_points
parameters.description: Number of points in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_prims
parameters.description: Number of primitives in this  SOP .

parameters.label: num_particles
parameters.description: Number of particles in this  SOP .

parameters.label: last_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating geometry data on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: last_meta_vbo_update_time
parameters.description: Time spent in another thread updating meta surface geometry data (such as metaballs or nurbs) on the  GPU  from the  SOP 's CPU data. As it is part of another thread, this time is not part of the usual frame time.

parameters.label: total_cooks
parameters.description: Number of times the operator has cooked since the process started.

parameters.label: cook_time
parameters.description: Duration of the last cook in milliseconds.

parameters.label: cook_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the component timeline.

parameters.label: cook_abs_frame
parameters.description: Frame number when this operator was last cooked relative to the absolute time.

parameters.label: cook_start_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator started cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cook_end_time
parameters.description: Time in milliseconds at which the operator finished cooking in the frame it was cooked.

parameters.label: cooked_this_frame
parameters.description: 1 if operator was cooked this frame.

parameters.label: warnings
parameters.description: Number of warnings in this operator if any.

parameters.label: errors
parameters.description: Number of errors in this operator if any.
